extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic article describing a historical broadcast hoax (the 1980 Great Blue Hill eruption April Fools' prank), its content, reactions, and consequences. The page summarizes events, public reaction, and regulatory/employment outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Communications Commission (FCC) rules on identifying stock footage
rubrics_metrics.description: The station was found to have violated the Federal Communications Commission's rules about showing stock footage without identifying it as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present stock or archival footage as live or local coverage without clear identification. In this incident, footage of Mount St. Helens was shown as if it depicted Great Blue Hill erupting, contributing to the deception and subsequent regulatory finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of good news judgment by broadcast producers
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive producer of the 6 o'clock news was fired for 'his failure to exercise good news judgment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and journalists should verify facts, avoid misleading editing (such as splicing or presenting unrelated footage or edited remarks as current), and consider potential public harm (e.g., causing panic) before airing material. The article cites use of edited presidential/governor remarks and unmarked stock footage as examples of poor judgment that led to public alarm and disciplinary action.
